title: Run declared plugin cleanup before removal
head: cba9e5d0399d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Open #10236 would execute a plugin's cleanup from the launcher with no hook-specific approval
leads.consequence: When a user confirms removing a launcher entry that #10236 recognizes as belonging to a plugin, that PR execs `omarchy-plugin-remove --yes <id>` in a detached process. This PR interprets --yes as authorization for the declared hook and passes it through, without showing another confirmation. Thus a launcher-deletion confirmation can trigger unsandboxed plugin code, including for a never-enabled plugin; the printed warning has no terminal in the AppLibrary detached path. Coordinate the callers or separate file-removal approval from approval to execute plugin code before both PRs merge.

leads.summary: Open #11069 adds an incompatible second plugin cleanup contract to the same remove/validate code
leads.consequence: #11069 independently adds mandatory `hooks.preRemove` with a separate --run-pre-remove authorization, no bypass and execution before disable. This PR adds `entryPoints.uninstall`, --skip-cleanup, --yes authorization and execution after disable. They are not stacked; git merge-file with the shared base produces four conflict hunks in remove's metadata, flags and cleanup region. A naïve combination cannot simultaneously preserve the advertised --skip-cleanup guarantee, the distinct authorization models and hook ordering; if both fields are configured, two cleanup executions are possible. Choose one contract or specify how both coexist before resolving conflicts.

leads.summary: Removal now rejects existing no-hook folders whose manifest lacks entryPoints, breaking open #13743's removal fixtures
leads.consequence: A regular plugin folder with an existing manifest but no `entryPoints` (or an invalid/nonobject entryPoints) used to be removable. The new helper rejects the manifest before confirmation despite the absence of any declared uninstall hook. `--skip-cleanup` is the recovery path, but #13743's unchanged test fixtures `acme.gone` and `acme.race` contain only an id and expect file removal and plugin-removed notification; both cases fail when the two PRs are combined, although the remove files themselves merge cleanly. Update that PR's fixtures to valid manifests before merging both, and document the explicit bypass required to remove preexisting broken folders rather than silently skipping a possibly declared hook.

leads.summary: Authoritative shell plugin references still claim every entry point is a QML Item and omit the new executable path
leads.consequence: The new manual links to the new hook contract, but the developer-facing manifest/installation references still say `Entry points are QML Items` (docs/omarchy-shell.md:42), document only QML kind entry points and discuss --yes as merely skipping prompts. Under the new contract, `entryPoints.uninstall` is an executable and `--yes` authorizes running it. A plugin author following the old full-schema reference could supply QML for uninstall or miss the code-execution implication. Update both shell references with the exception and link to the contract.

leads.summary: Uninstall path validator accepts C1 control characters despite its documented control-character ban
leads.consequence: The predicate rejects code points under 32 and DEL (127), but not Unicode C1 controls U+0080–U+009F. A manifest path ending in `\u0085` (with a matching executable file) is accepted and returned to the confirmation prompt. These characters can misrender or obscure the disclosed pathname. Reject C1 too, or narrow the documentation to the controls actually refused; add a representative test in the unsafe-entry loop.

leads.summary: New remove tests never check that a different valid declared executable is the one run
leads.consequence: Every successful fixture declares `bin/cleanup`; unsafe names are rejected but no valid alternative path is tested. A mistaken implementation that validates the declared path, then returns `bin/cleanup` regardless, keeps all 12 existing assertions passing yet would execute the wrong program for real plugins declaring another executable. Add a second valid executable with distinct side effects and assert only the declared one runs (and is named in confirmation).

limits: Only pinned source and synthetic sandbox files were executed. The full test/cli exits before reaching its metadata loop in this sandbox because a theme fixture is missing; metadata and dispatcher values for the changed commands were checked separately (lab/runs/20261001T050642Z-48dcd1ea).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Some plugins without an uninstall hook now need `--skip-cleanup` to be removed.

### Some plugins without a hook are refused

`omarchy-plugin-uninstall-path` (lines 22-24) requires a regular manifest with an `entryPoints` object before checking whether `uninstall` is declared, and removal calls it for every non-symlinked folder with a `manifest.json` unless `--skip-cleanup` is given. A manifest without `entryPoints` (e.g. `{"id":"acme.legacy"}`) or a symlinked `manifest.json` fails with `invalid uninstall entry point`; the merge base removed it. **Impact:** this contradicts `docs/plugin-uninstall.md` ("Plugins without the entry point keep the existing removal behavior") and breaks the remove tests of open #13743.

**Suggested change:** after refusing unparseable JSON, exit 0 unless `try (.entryPoints | has("uninstall")) catch false` holds, and only then require a regular manifest.

<details><summary>Reproducer: hookless plugin refused (fails at cba9e5d0)</summary>

Reproducer: removal now refuses a hookless plugin whose manifest has no entryPoints object

Test file in the style of `test/shell.d/plugin-remove-test.sh` (save as `test/shell.d/plugin-remove-legacy-test.sh`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
require_command jq

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$test_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$test_dir/stubs"
cat >"$test_dir/stubs/omarchy-shell" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $2 == "listPlugins" ]] && echo '[]'
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$test_dir/stubs/omarchy-shell"

# A leftover folder whose manifest the shell never accepted (no entryPoints
# object), so it declares no uninstall entry point.
plugin="$test_dir/home/.config/omarchy/plugins/acme.legacy"
mkdir -p "$plugin/.git"
printf '{"id":"acme.legacy"}\n' >"$plugin/manifest.json"

output=$(HOME="$test_dir/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$test_dir/stubs:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-plugin-remove" acme.legacy --yes 2>&1) ||
  fail "a plugin without an uninstall entry point is removed as before" "$output"
[[ ! -e $plugin ]] || fail "the plugin folder is removed"
pass "a plugin without an uninstall entry point is removed as before"
```

Output at the PR head (cba9e5d0399d47301bb14e33e5afb79d939d967f), `bash test/shell.d/plugin-remove-legacy-test.sh`, exit 1:

```
omarchy-plugin-uninstall-path: invalid manifest
omarchy-plugin-remove: invalid uninstall entry point; inspect it or use --skip-cleanup to remove without running plugin code
not ok - a plugin without an uninstall entry point is removed as before
```

Output at the merge base (31bd80daa4613ffdee995ac27467fce5a2990806), exit 0:

```
ok - a plugin without an uninstall entry point is removed as before
```

Output at the head with the suggested helper change (check for `entryPoints.uninstall` before requiring an `entryPoints` object), exit 0; the PR's own `plugin-remove-test.sh` (12 checks) and `plugin-validate-test.sh` also pass with that change:

```
ok - a plugin without an uninstall entry point is removed as before
```

The same refusal makes open PR #13743's `test/shell.d/plugin-lifecycle-hooks-test.sh` fail when both PRs are merged onto quattro 8b4eae66 (its fixtures use `{"id":"acme.gone"}` manifests). Actual output on the combined tree, exit 1:

```
ok - plugin add fires plugin-added once the clone is in place
ok - plugin-added fires before the shell rescan
ok - plugin add fires no plugin-added when the add fails
ok - plugin-added fires before the rescan and the optional enable
omarchy-plugin-uninstall-path: invalid manifest
omarchy-plugin-remove: invalid uninstall entry point; inspect it or use --skip-cleanup to remove without running plugin code
not ok - plugin remove succeeds
```

On quattro plus #13743 alone the same file passes all 9 checks.

</details>

<details><summary>Related open PRs</summary>

- #11069 (same title) proposes a different cleanup contract (`hooks.preRemove`, `--run-pre-remove`, no bypass, cleanup before disable) It conflicts with this PR in `bin/omarchy-plugin-remove` and `manual/32-shell-plugins.md`, and both add a hook check to `bin/omarchy-plugin-validate`. The two need one agreed contract.
- #10236 makes launcher-entry removal run `exec omarchy-plugin-remove --yes "$plugin_id"`. With this PR, that `--yes` also approves running a declared hook, with no hook-specific prompt.
- #13743: besides the fixture failure above, the exact event-order assertion in the new test fails on the combined tree, because #13743 calls `omarchy-shell -q shell rescanPlugins`.
- #13913 makes the same must-be-`ok` disable change on the same lines (textual conflict).

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (at cba9e5d0, synthetic HOME, stubbed `omarchy-shell` and `gum`):
- Order is disable, revalidate, hook, remove or back up, rescan; the hook runs in the plugin directory with both environment variables set.
- A failed hook keeps the files and skips the rescan, and a retry completes. A disable answer other than `ok` stops before the hook.
- Non-interactive removal without `--yes`, `--skip-cleanup` and symlinked folders run no plugin code.
- The new test passes 12/12 at the head and fails on the base code; the existing plugin suites pass.

**Optional notes:**
- **Optional test improvement:** removing `$entry != *..*` from the helper leaves all 12 checks passing, because the `../outside` and `bin/../cleanup` cases point at files that do not exist. A case with an existing target catches it (reproducer below).
- Declining the combined prompt aborts with `omarchy-plugin-remove: aborted` and does not mention `--skip-cleanup`, and the Setup > Plugins > Remove menu passes no flags. Naming the flag in the decline message would show a way forward.
- `docs/omarchy-shell.md` on the base branch `quattro` says "Entry points are QML `Item`s" (line 52) and that `--yes` skips every prompt (line 91). Mentioning the uninstall hook there would tell plugin authors that this entry point is an executable and that `--yes` now also approves running it.

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: untested `..` guard (passes at cba9e5d0, fails on the mutant)</summary>

Reproducer: the `..` guard in omarchy-plugin-uninstall-path is not exercised by the PR's test

This is a test-strength note, not a behaviour bug: at the PR head the guard works. The PR's traversal cases (`"../outside"`, `"bin/../cleanup"`) point at files that do not exist, so they are rejected by the final `-f`/`-x` check whether or not the `..` check is present.

Mutation used (one line in `bin/omarchy-plugin-uninstall-path`):

```diff
-[[ $entry != /* && $entry != *..* && $entry != */ && $entry != *//* ]] || fail "uninstall entry point must be a safe relative path"
+[[ $entry != /* && $entry != */ && $entry != *//* ]] || fail "uninstall entry point must be a safe relative path"
```

With that mutation, the PR's `bash test/shell.d/plugin-remove-test.sh` still passes all 12 checks (exit 0):

```
ok - approved cleanup runs in the plugin directory before removal and rescan
ok - failed cleanup keeps the plugin for retry and a retry completes
ok - non-interactive removal without --yes executes no plugin code
ok - IPC-level disable failure cannot be mistaken for successful unload
ok - explicit cleanup bypass removes broken plugins without running code
ok - plugins without hooks retain existing backup behavior
ok - symlinked plugins are unlinked without executing their code
ok - unsafe paths, control characters and invalid hook types are rejected
ok - both executable and parent symlinks are rejected
ok - install and removal enforce the same executable hook contract
ok - recursive self-removal fails before cleanup
ok - interactive confirmation discloses execution and cancellation runs no code
```

A case whose escape target exists catches it (save as `test/shell.d/plugin-remove-escape-test.sh`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
require_command jq

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$test_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$test_dir/stubs"
cat >"$test_dir/stubs/omarchy-shell" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $2 == "listPlugins" ]] && echo '[]'
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$test_dir/stubs/omarchy-shell"

# The escape target exists and is executable, so only the '..' guard can
# reject it.
home="$test_dir/home"
plugins="$home/.config/omarchy/plugins"
plugin="$plugins/acme.test"
mkdir -p "$plugin"
touch "$plugin/Widget.qml" "$home/external-setup"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nrm -- "$HOME/external-setup"\n' >"$plugins/outside"
chmod +x "$plugins/outside"
printf '%s\n' '{"schemaVersion":1,"id":"acme.test","name":"Test","version":"1","kinds":["bar-widget"],"entryPoints":{"barWidget":"Widget.qml","uninstall":"../outside"}}' >"$plugin/manifest.json"

output=$(HOME="$home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$test_dir/stubs:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-plugin-remove" acme.test --yes 2>&1) &&
  fail "an existing parent-directory hook path is rejected" "$output"
[[ -f $home/external-setup && -f $plugin/manifest.json ]] ||
  fail "an escaping hook never runs"
pass "an existing parent-directory hook path is rejected"
```

At the PR head, exit 0:

```
ok - an existing parent-directory hook path is rejected
```

With the mutation above, exit 1 (the outside script ran and the plugin was removed):

```
Cleanup executes unsandboxed plugin code. Review it before approving.
Running cleanup for acme.test...
Cleanup completed for acme.test.
Removed acme.test. Backup at: /tmp/tmp.UHDX7KGWXb/home/.config/omarchy/plugins/.acme.test.bak.20261001051831
not ok - an existing parent-directory hook path is rejected
```

</details>
